title: AI Brief — Thursday, 5 November 2026
summary: Open-weights day — Moonshot dropped the Kimi K3.1 Pro weights (2.8T MoE, 1M context), Ricursive's dense Ripple-65B claims the US open-weight lead on agentic coding and Tencent shipped Hy4 with weights promised "in the coming days", while Anthropic showed you can cryptographically prove which model produced an answer.

items.title: Weight-Space Programming: an LLM reads and edits neural-net weights directly (Takehi, Teoh, Zhang, Khattab — MIT CSAIL)
items.summary: A frontier LLM identified what small networks do from raw weights alone, wrote game-playing MLPs from scratch that beat PPO baselines, and lifted Qwen3.5-0.8B from 7.9% to 48.1% on MATH-500 by editing 0.016% of its weights — no gradient descent involved. The authors call it "very early"; the gain on Qwen came mostly from removing a looping failure mode, and the same trick failed on Gemma 3 270M. Still the most-discussed research of the week and a new way to think about model repair.

items.title: FlashProve: Anthropic's "provable inference" — a zkSNARK that proves which weights produced a response
items.summary: A provider commits to a set of weights and emits a proof that each response came from them; a verifier checks it in ~17 s on a CPU without seeing the weights. On Llama 4 Maverick (400B MoE, 4-bit) one H100 proves ~110 tok/s, at 70–95× the GPU time of plain vLLM inference, with a 19 MB proof per 1,024-token request. This is the first practical path to verifying that an API or router is serving the model you paid for. Code, a C++ verifier and Lean proofs are Apache 2.0. Caveats: greedy decoding, integer model, 1,024-token context.

items.title: Route Anything: a study of model and policy routing for general-purpose AI systems
items.summary: Builds a 374k-run trajectory matrix across 25 benchmarks and 452 candidate models/tools/policies, then trains routers. Per-input oracle routing beats the best single candidate by 5.4 points; learned routers give modest quality gains at ~24% less policy time and ~8.8× better efficiency on average. Useful if you are deciding between a single big model and a router in production.

items.title: Think Less, Locally (LoCo): local preference learning to stop reasoning models overthinking
items.summary: Finds the point where a reasoning model should have stopped, generates shorter verified continuations from that state and trains with DPO on the pairs. Reasoning length drops 42–45% on math and 23–36% on code (trained on math only) with accuracy held or improved. A cheap recipe if you fine-tune reasoning models and pay per token.

items.title: ToolSpace: synthesising tool-use environments from real MCP traces for long-horizon agents
items.summary: Mines tool-call dependencies from real MCP execution traces (deterministic rules, no LLM judge), clusters them into environments, then random-walks to generate verifiable tasks. Training on it lifts Qwen3.6-35B-A3B from 23.0 to 41.0 average across seven tool-use benchmarks, and GLM-5.2 to roughly Claude Opus 5 level. Relevant if you build agent training data or evals.

items.title: Simon Willison reproduces the weight-reading task on a laptop with Qwen 3.8 27B
items.summary: Q4_K_M in LM Studio identified 3 of 4 games from raw policy weights, but each run took 45–65 minutes and ~40k reasoning tokens; Kimi K3.1 Pro did it in under 10 minutes. His take: real, but a patient human with pencil and paper could do the same, so the hype is overdone.

items.title: MEMENTO: learning context management for long-context agents
items.summary: Trains an agent to compress its own history into notes, keeping the working context under 20k tokens on book-length QA. A trained alternative to hand-rolled compaction heuristics.

items.title: Fidelity collapses with table size, not turn count (deployed tool-using agent)
items.summary: Feeding large tool outputs (big tables) straight into the planner's context is what degrades accuracy, not conversation length; delivering results through a side channel avoids it. A concrete architecture lesson for data-pipeline agents.

items.title: Embedding Semantic Entropy: NLI-free hallucination detection
items.summary: Clusters sampled responses by embedding similarity instead of running an entailment model, matching semantic-entropy performance at a fraction of the cost. Easy to bolt onto an existing RAG eval loop.

items.title: deepseek-ai/dsh-superagent-prototype
items.summary: DeepSeek Harness team's MIT-licensed "proactive coding agent": it listens to GitHub (and optionally Feishu), turns authorised requests into work items, runs each in its own directory and agent session, and replies with a PR; a web panel surfaces anything needing a human. DeepSeek reports p95 task completion falling from 29.5 to 15.7 minutes versus a single session with subagents. Caveat from the README: largely agent-written, review before running.
items.note: point it at one repo and let it work issues in parallel while you review PRs.

items.title: RikiyaT/lm_understand-logs — code and logs behind Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: The experiment logs and code for the week's most talked-about result, plus an edited Qwen3.5-0.8B checkpoint on Hugging Face and a live demo Space.
items.note: replay the game-identification and weight-edit experiments, or hand the raw weights of your own small model to an LLM and see what it infers.

items.title: storytold/craft-anything
items.summary: Studies an existing website, app or game (screenshots, layout, optionally code), has your coding agent rebuild it in the stack you ask for, then diffs the result against the original until it converges. 320 analysis tools exposed as both CLI and MCP. Early alpha; the README limits it to software you own or are allowed to examine.
items.note: port a legacy internal tool to a new framework, or use the MCP tools as a reusable "inspect this UI" toolkit for your own agents.

items.title: KKKKhazix/agent-autoloop
items.summary: Self-hosted hub that lets a CLI agent (Claude Code, Codex, ACP, or any command) pick up work from cron, GitHub events or HTTP, and only interrupts you with an approval card (Slack, Discord, Feishu, desktop) when it is unsure, then resumes the same session. Includes a PR delivery pipeline: review → wait for CI → merge → verify deploy. ~1,650-line kernel, no runtime deps, MIT.
items.note: wire nightly data-pipeline checks or issue triage to an agent that runs unattended and pings you only for decisions.

items.title: Balanov/uncut
items.summary: A deliberately minimal headless coding-agent harness: one 7 MB static binary, four tools, stdin/stdout, no compaction or truncation — if the provider cuts output it exits non-zero instead of pretending. Works with any OpenAI-compatible endpoint including Ollama.
items.note: `git diff | uncut "Review this diff"` in CI, with `--json` NDJSON events and resumable JSONL sessions.

items.title: caru-ini/stack-diagram
items.summary: An agent skill: describe your stack in one sentence and get an architecture diagram with official logos. Handy for docs and design reviews.

items.title: datasette-agent 0.5a0 and datasette-apps 0.3a0
items.summary: Simon Willison's Datasette agent now keeps a chat panel beside your data pages and can build/edit custom HTML apps over stored queries, with approval gates on write queries. A worked example of an agent living inside a data tool rather than beside it.

items.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro weights — 2.8T-parameter MoE, 104B active, 1M context, natively multimodal
items.summary: The model that topped Vals' October open-weight ranking is now self-hostable: MoE with 896 experts (16 routed + 2 shared), KDA plus gated sparse attention for long context, MXFP4 weights from quantisation-aware training, MoonViT-V2 vision encoder. Serve with vLLM or SGLang; `reasoning_effort` low/high/max; Huawei announced Ascend support. Licence is a custom "Kimi K3.1 Pro License", so read it before commercial use. Weights are ~1.5 TB, so this is for clusters, not laptops.
items.source: Hugging Face model card, TechNode (5 Nov), HN 514 pts

items.title: OpenAI to acquire Pierre Computer Company to build out Codex's repo and review layer
items.summary: Pierre makes a Code Storage service plus the open-source Trees and Diffs libraries that Codex already uses for file-tree navigation and visual diffs; terms undisclosed, open-source projects stay public. Together with OpenAI's internal Pando source-control backend, it points at Codex becoming an end-to-end repository and review environment rather than a tool that sits on top of GitHub.
items.source: openai.com, Yahoo Finance, The Information (4 Nov)

items.title: Tencent launches Hy4 with vision and computer use; weights "in the coming days"
items.summary: 770B total / 49B active, 1M context, first Hy model that can drive CLI and GUI (trained on Blender and CAD workflows). Tencent reports hallucination rate down from 12.95% to 7.2% versus the Preview and a lead over DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi K3.1 Pro in a 213-analyst blind financial-analysis eval. Available now on Tencent Cloud TokenHub and OpenRouter at ~$0.90/$2.70 per M tokens; a Flash variant is coming.

items.title: IEEE Spectrum: "AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt" (the PHP2Shell story)
items.summary: An out-of-memory bug reported to PHP in 2024 and shelved became remote code execution within two weeks once an AI-assisted researcher looked at it; a four-person team then needed two months to patch it. The argument — AI makes finding bugs far cheaper than fixing them, which lands hardest on open-source maintainers — is the top HN thread today at 1,100+ points.
items.source: IEEE Spectrum (2 Nov, updated 4 Nov), HN

items.title: Ask HN: What's your current AI agentic setup?
items.summary: A 300+ point, 300+ comment snapshot of what developers actually pay for and run: subscriptions vs OpenRouter vs local, which harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Pi, Aider, Hermes) and why they switched. Worth ten minutes if you are reconsidering your own stack.

items.title: Latent Space AI News (3 Nov) — the full weekend roundup
items.summary: Includes items this brief did not independently verify: SemiAnalysis' GDPx economic-task eval (best model 12%), Qwen's statement that it will stay open-weight through Qwen 4 and 5, and MiniMax M3.1 Flash community quants. Treat the X/Reddit-sourced items as unverified.

items.title: Ripple-65B Preview — dense 65B open-weight model, 80.52 on Terminal-Bench 2.1
items.summary: From Ricursive Intelligence (an AI chip-design lab); a dense Transformer pretrained on 12T tokens with 1M context, which the company calls US open-weight SOTA on agentic coding, ahead of Reflection Beam 501B (80.1) and Muse Spark Open 816B (76.4) at roughly a tenth of the training cost (~$32M). At 65B dense it runs on a DGX Spark or a high-memory MacBook Pro, which none of the 500B+ open models do. Licence not stated on the page; available on Hugging Face, Together, OpenRouter and GMI Cloud.

items.title: Tencent Hy4 — 770B/49B-active, vision + computer use, API live now
items.summary: The first open-weights-track model from a major lab with native computer use, priced at ~$0.90 in / $2.70 out per million tokens (50% off on Tencent Cloud through December). Weights and system cards are promised within days; two research models built on it (HyCell for single-cell biology, HyPDE for physics fields) are already open.

items.title: OpenAI API: GPT-Image-2.6 Flare and Sunburst (Images 2.6)
items.summary: Two new image models on `v1/images/generations` and `v1/images/edits` with adjustable complexity, native SVG and animated GIF output, and markup-guided editing; OpenAI says generation is ~50% faster. Images 2.6 also rolls out in ChatGPT and Codex with reference images.

items.title: Claude API: Message threads beta — server-side conversation state
items.summary: With the `message-threads-2026-08-12` header the API keeps the conversation on the server and each request sends only new messages; threads expire 5 minutes after the last request and are deleted within an hour. Cuts payload size and client-side bookkeeping for agent loops. Available on the Claude API, AWS, Google Cloud (Anthropic-managed) and Microsoft Foundry.

items.title: vLLM v0.33.0
items.summary: Adds Reflection Beam-1.0 and Muse Spark Open, moves to PyTorch 2.14 and CUDA 13.0 by default (12.9 wheels dropped), plus speculative-decoding and NVIDIA decode speedups. Breaking: Medusa, the MLP speculator and the legacy Ray compiled-graph executor are removed — check your serving configs before upgrading.

items.title: Claude API: text watermark now on Mythos 5, Opus 4.7 and Sonnet 4.6 output
items.summary: Generated text carries Anthropic's text watermark on the listed platforms; on Sonnet 4.6, non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` may skip it. Relevant if you post-process or detect model output in pipelines.

items.title: Running Kimi K3.1 Pro yourself: the practical bits
items.summary: The model card recommends vLLM, SGLang or TokenSpeed with an OpenAI-compatible endpoint; set `reasoning_effort` (default "max"), and for multi-turn tool use pass back the full assistant message including `reasoning_content` and `tool_calls`, not just `content`. Transformers works with `trust_remote_code=True`.

items.title: Gemini API changelog: no new entries since 30 Oct
items.summary: Nothing shipped in the Gemini API over the last five days; checked so you don't have to.

items.title: Weight-Space Programming — treating a model's weights as something an LLM can read and patch
items.summary:
The idea is simple: hand a capable LLM the raw parameters of a small network (a policy MLP, a tiny diffusion model, a layer of a small LM) as text, and ask it to reason about what the network does, or to propose a targeted edit, with no gradients and sometimes no forward passes. It sits between mechanistic interpretability (which usually needs activations and tooling) and fine-tuning (which needs data and an optimiser), and the striking results this week — a 0.016% weight edit that quadrupled a 0.8B model's MATH-500 score — came from the LLM spotting a looping pathology and switching it off, not from teaching new skills.

It matters now because it reframes model repair and auditing as a language task: you could ask an agent "why does this policy fail?" or "is this checkpoint sycophantic?" and get an answer grounded in the parameters. The critiques are as instructive as the results — a frontier model couldn't detect sycophancy from Gemma weights alone, the edit failed on a model that doesn't loop, and Simon Willison's local reproduction showed a 27B model can do the easy cases slowly. Expect "weight-reading" benchmarks and harnesses to appear quickly; the authors say they are building one.
